about: The behavioural corpus for the bridge's PORT of agent-board-toolkit's plain-language card-text checks (card#11987). The toolkit OWNS the rules — titles T1-T6, the description's filing bar (the IMPACT line) and D1 — and declares them once, in bin/_card-text-rules.json; `kbcard` reads that file, and the bridge vendors it verbatim (resources/card-text-rules.json) and reads it in PHP, because board_create_card and board_correct_card must refuse exactly the text `kbcard` refuses, with the same words. What is compared is the WHOLE refusal text after kbcard's `kbcard: ` prefix — the verdict, the findings, the suggested rewrite — or null for text that passes. tests/Unit/Support/CardTextParityTest.php runs every vector against the port on every test run; bin/card-text-parity.sh runs the same vectors against a toolkit checkout's own kbcard.

authority.symbol: kbcard title-check / kbcard description-check (_kbc_title_bar, _kbc_mint_bar) over bin/_card-text-rules.json
authority.relationship: The toolkit OWNS these rules (its README § "Plain-language card text" states them and § "The rule file's schema" defines the matching for a non-bash reader). The port follows kbcard's ACTUAL behaviour wherever a PCRE reader can — what a seat is told by the CLI — and where it cannot, follows the README and publishes the pair under known_divergences for the toolkit to settle. Any other disagreement is the bridge's defect to fix by re-porting.

how_the_far_end_runs_this: From a bridge checkout: `bin/card-text-parity.sh --corpus docs/card-text-parity-corpus.json --toolkit <toolkit git checkout>`. Each vector's first argument goes to that checkout's `bin/kbcard title-check --name` (method `title`) or `description-check --description` (method `description`), in a sandbox HOME with no KB_TITLE_BAR / KB_MINT_BAR; rc 0 is null, rc 2 is its stderr less the `kbcard: ` prefix and the final newline, which must equal `expect` byte for byte. The second and third arguments are the verb and tail kbcard's dry run prints, and are checked, not sent. SOURCE_COMMIT / SOURCE_SHA256 are checked against the checkout's git history and the bridge's vendored file. Exit 0 agreed, 1 drifted, 2 could not measure. `--control` perturbs every expectation and constant and must report each one.
not_checked_by_this_repo: NOTHING IN THIS REPO'S CI RUNS THE TOOLKIT: a change to kbcard or to its rule file reds nothing here until someone runs bin/card-text-parity.sh against the changed toolkit. Run it on a toolkit bump. This repo's suite does check that the vendored bytes still hash to SOURCE_SHA256.

The check is VECTOR-granular: a rule, or a branch of kbcard, that no published vector reaches is invisible to both ends. POSIX ERE leftmost-longest and PCRE backtracking can differ in ways the port's load-time alternation guard does not cover; only the vectors hold those.

A BLANK title or description never reaches the rules at either end, so no vector carries one: kbcard refuses it as holding no text, and the bridge refuses a blank title with its own `title` refusal and treats a blank description as absent.
The rule file's `tags` block is not read by the bridge; tag policy is CallerTagPolicy's.

last_measured.method: `bin/card-text-parity.sh --corpus docs/card-text-parity-corpus.json --toolkit <that checkout>` sent every vector through that checkout's kbcard and checked both pinned constants (the rule file is unchanged since SOURCE_COMMIT, so the pin still holds); `--control` was run on the same checkout and reported every perturbed expectation. A copy of that checkout with T1's limit edited to 79 was reported as DRIFTED (exit 1), so the runner is seen to fail on a changed rule. The same corpus run against the pre-fix kbcard (c4c7fa65) reported the trailing-dash title vectors (`flag --x-`, `--x--`, `--flag-`) as DRIFTED (exit 1): those vectors are what would catch kbcard cutting the trailing `-` again.
last_measured.result: Exit 0: every vector and both pinned constants agreed; no known divergence is published. Whoever adds, changes or deletes a vector re-takes this measurement over the WHOLE corpus and re-writes vectors_digest — CardTextParityTest reds when the digest no longer matches.
